questions.stem: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area (~342,239 sq km), followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. Uttar Pradesh is the largest by population. Goa is the smallest state by area.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga (~2,525 km) is the longest river flowing within India. The Godavari (~1,465 km) is the longest river of peninsular India (the 'Dakshin Ganga'). The Brahmaputra is longer overall but most of its length is outside India. The Indus is longer still but largely flows through Pakistan.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the highest mountain peak in the world?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest (8,849 m) in the Himalayas (Nepal-China border) is the highest peak above sea level. K2 (8,611 m) is the second-highest; Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is the third-highest and the highest peak in India (Sikkim). Note: Mauna Kea is taller base-to-peak, but Everest is highest above sea level.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of Earth's surface (~165 million sq km). It contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth. Order by size: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic (smallest).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile (~6,650 km) in Africa is traditionally regarded as the longest river in the world, though some studies argue the Amazon (~6,400 km) may be longer depending on measurement of its source. The Yangtze (Asia's longest, ~6,300 km) is third. The Amazon is by far the largest by water volume/discharge.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: By the strict definition (low precipitation), the Antarctic Polar Desert is the largest desert in the world (~14 million sq km). Among hot deserts, the Sahara (~9.2 million sq km) is the largest. The Thar Desert is India's largest. Many quizzes accept Sahara if 'hot desert' is specified — read the question carefully.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world (~0.49 sq km), an enclave within Rome and the seat of the Catholic Church. Monaco is the second-smallest. Nauru is the smallest island nation. By contrast, Russia is the largest country by area.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the highest waterfall in India?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls (Karnataka, ~455 m) is generally regarded as the highest waterfall in India. Jog Falls (Karnataka) is the highest plunge (single-drop) waterfall and more famous. Nohkalikai Falls (Meghalaya) is the tallest plunge waterfall by some measures. Dudhsagar is on the Goa-Karnataka border.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir) is the largest freshwater lake in India. Chilika Lake (Odisha) is the largest brackish/coastal lagoon in India (and largest in Asia). Loktak Lake (Manipur) is famous for its floating phumdis. Dal Lake (Srinagar) is famous for tourism but smaller.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest continent in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent (~44.6 million sq km, ~30% of Earth's land), and also the most populous. Order by area: Asia > Africa > North America > South America > Antarctica > Europe > Australia (smallest). Australia is the smallest continent; Antarctica is the least populated.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the most populous country in the world (as of 2023)?
questions.explanation: India became the most populous country in the world in 2023, surpassing China, with over 1.42 billion people (UN estimates). China is now second. The US, Indonesia, and Pakistan round out the top five. India's population is younger, with a large working-age share (the 'demographic dividend').
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland (and largest internal organ) in the human body, weighing ~1.5 kg. It performs functions like bile production, detoxification, and glycogen storage. The skin is the largest organ overall. The pituitary is the 'master gland' but is tiny; the thyroid is the largest pure endocrine gland.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, with a diameter ~11 times that of Earth and more mass than all other planets combined. Saturn is second-largest (famous for its rings). The smallest planet is Mercury. Jupiter has the most known moons and the Great Red Spot (a giant storm).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the most populous city / urban agglomeration in India?
questions.explanation: Mumbai (Greater Mumbai) is generally the most populous city proper in India, while the Delhi urban agglomeration is the largest metropolitan area and is projected to become the world's most populous city. Both are very close; exam answers often expect Mumbai for 'most populous city' and Delhi for 'largest metro/NCR'. Mumbai is also India's financial capital.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the longest national highway in India?
questions.explanation: NH 44 is the longest national highway in India (~3,745 km), running north-south from Srinagar (J&K) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu). It was formed by merging several older highways. NH 27 is the longest east-west highway. (Highway numbering was rationalised in 2010.)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The stapes ('stirrup'), located in the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the human body (~3 mm). It is one of the three ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) that transmit sound vibrations. The femur (thigh bone) is the largest and strongest bone.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest mammal in the world?
questions.explanation: The Blue Whale is the largest mammal — and the largest animal ever known to have lived — reaching ~30 m and ~180 tonnes. The African bush elephant is the largest land mammal. The giraffe is the tallest land animal. The blue whale's heart alone can weigh ~180 kg.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states (~1,600 km / ~2,340 km by some measures). Andhra Pradesh has the second longest, followed by Tamil Nadu. Among all Indian coastal regions, the union territory areas and the mainland total ~7,500 km. Gujarat's long, indented coastline supports major ports like Kandla and Mundra.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the deepest point in the world's oceans?
questions.explanation: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench (western Pacific) is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans, ~10,935 m (about 11 km) below sea level — deeper than Mount Everest is tall. The Tonga Trench is the second deepest. The Java (Sunda) Trench is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest river island in the world, located in India?
questions.explanation: Majuli, on the Brahmaputra River in Assam, is the largest river island in the world (it shrank over time due to erosion but remains the largest). In 2016 Majuli became the first island to be made a district in India. It is a centre of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture (Satras). Srirangam (Tamil Nadu) is a notable river island too.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the highest battlefield in the world, where the Indian Army maintains a presence?
questions.explanation: The Siachen Glacier (Karakoram range, ~5,400+ m / up to ~6,700 m at posts) is the highest battlefield in the world, where India and Pakistan have maintained military presence since Operation Meghdoot (1984). The extreme altitude and cold cause more casualties than combat. Galwan Valley and Doklam are India-China friction points.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest brackish water lagoon in Asia?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake (Odisha) is the largest brackish water lagoon in Asia and the second-largest coastal lagoon in the world. It is a Ramsar site and a haven for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins. Vembanad (Kerala) is India's longest lake; Pulicat (TN-AP) is the second-largest brackish lagoon in India.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the tallest statue in the world?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India (182 m, depicting Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, unveiled 2018) is the tallest statue in the world. The Spring Temple Buddha in China (~128 m) is second. The Statue of Liberty (~93 m with pedestal) and Christ the Redeemer (~38 m) are much shorter.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Russia is the largest country in the world by area (~17.1 million sq km), spanning 11 time zones across Europe and Asia. Canada is second, the USA and China are close third/fourth. India is the seventh-largest country by area. Russia's area is nearly twice that of Canada.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the highest-altitude lake in India (among these well-known lakes)?
questions.explanation: Cholamu (Tso Lhamo) Lake in Sikkim, at ~5,330 m, is among the highest lakes in India and the world, near the source of the Teesta River. Pangong Tso (~4,350 m) and Tso Moriri (~4,520 m) in Ladakh are famous high-altitude lakes; Chandratal (~4,300 m) is in Himachal Pradesh. Cholamu is the highest of these.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
